newsitem.title: USA: Payments system's role key - St. Louis Fed' Melzer.
newsitem.headline: Payments system's role key - St. Louis Fed' Melzer.

text.p: - Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Thomas Melzer said on Friday confidence in U.S. monetary authority and the payments system is key to long-term growth.
"For our nation to achieve maximum sustainable growth, users of the payments system must have confidence in the monetary authority," Melzer told a symposium at the University of Missouri-St. Louis.
Three other Fed bank presidents also addressed the symposium on the challenges facing the banking industry due to new technology.
Melzer, who described the payments system as "a communication network," stressed one key role of the central bank is to preserve the value of the currency.

"The growth of the monetary base is determined solely by the Federal Reserve's actions," Melzer said. "In the long run, a symbiotic relationship exists between the Federal Reserve's payments system and monetary policy roles."
Melzer stressed "appropriate growth of the monetary base is essential for price stability, which fosters maximum growth."
However, Melzer acknowledged the challenges to controlling the monetary base stemming from new technology, such as electronic money.

"The major point I want to make today is this -- Every potential change to the payments system must be evaluated as to whether the holder of a particular payment instrument can convert that instrument base money on demand," Melzer said.
